366852.title: Locally series-parallel graph characterization conjecture
366852.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a possibly infinite graph and let $r\geqslant 3$ be an integer. A graph is **$r$-locally series-parallel** when each of its $r/2$-balls is series-parallel, and an **$r$-local subdivision** of a wheel or of $K_4$ is a subdivision $H$ of a wheel or $K_4$ contained in $B_H(v,r/2)$ for some vertex $v$ of $H$. Let $G_r$ denote the $r$-local cover of $G$.

**Locally series-parallel graph characterization conjecture.** The following are equivalent:

1. $G$ is $r$-locally series-parallel.
2. $G$ does not contain an $r$-local subdivision of a wheel or of a $K_4$.
3. $G_r$ is series-parallel.

This conjecture seeks a characterization of locally series-parallel graphs analogous to the corresponding characterizations for locally acyclic and locally chordal graphs. Series-parallel graphs are precisely the graphs of treewidth at most $2$, while the conjectured forbidden local subdivisions reflect the role of $K_4$ and wheels in this setting. The source provides no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

373016.title: The unpinning avoidance game PSPACE-completeness conjecture
373016.literal_statement:
Let $\gamma\colon\bigsqcup_{i=1}^s S^1\looparrowright\Sigma$ be a multiloop on a surface $\Sigma$. In the unpinning avoidance game, two players alternately remove pins while leaving a pinning set after each turn; the first player with no legal move loses. Let $\mathsf{Unpin_{AVOID}}(\Sigma,s)$ be the decision problem asking whether Player 1 has a winning strategy, and let $\mathsf{SimpleUnpin_{AVOID}}(\Sigma,s)$ be its restriction to simple multiloops.

**Unpinning avoidance game complexity conjecture.** The problem $\mathsf{Unpin_{AVOID}}(\Sigma,s)$ is $\textsf{PSPACE}$-complete for any $s$ and $\Sigma$, and $\mathsf{SimpleUnpin_{AVOID}}(\Sigma,s)$ is $\textsf{PSPACE}$-complete for any $s\geq 4$.

The conjecture is motivated by the relationship with Node Kayles, which is known to be $\textsf{PSPACE}$-complete, but the paper leaves these game-complexity claims unresolved.

373251.title: Song–Wang's cyclotomic RSK bijection conjecture
373251.literal_statement:
For a level $\ell$ and multipartition data $\mu,\nu$, let $\mathrm{ParMat}_{\nu,\mu}^{\flat}$ denote the corresponding set of enriched block matrices, let $\mathrm{SST}_{\ell}(\lambda,\mu)$ denote the set of level-$\ell$ semistandard tableaux of shape $\lambda$ and content $\mu$, and let $\lambda \vdash_{\ell} n$ range over level-$\ell$ multipartitions of $n$. **Song–Wang's conjecture.** There exists, for each level $\ell$, a combinatorial bijection

$$
\psi_\ell: \mathrm{ParMat}_{\nu,\mu}^{\flat} \longrightarrow \bigsqcup_{\lambda \vdash_\ell n} \mathrm{SST}_\ell(\lambda,\mu)\times \mathrm{SST}_\ell(\lambda,\nu),
$$

which extends the level $\ell-1$ bijection and recovers the classical RSK correspondence when $\ell=1$. This conjecture proposes a cyclotomic analogue of the classical RSK correspondence, relating the block-matrix basis data in the cyclotomic web category to pairs of tableaux in the cyclotomic Schur algebra; its status is not established in the supplied text.

374302.title: The saturation conjecture for Markov polynomials
374302.literal_statement:
Let $\rho=\frac{a}{b}\frac{}{}$ be a rational number in $[0,1]$, and write the numerator of its Markov polynomial as

$$
P_{\rho}(u,v,w)=\sum A_{ij}u^iv^jw^{a+b-1-i-j}.
$$

Its Newton polygon is

$$
\Delta_{\rho}=\operatorname{Conv}\lbrace(i,j):A_{ij}\neq 0\rbrace.
$$

**Saturation conjecture.** The terms that appear in the numerator of a Markov polynomial $M_{\rho}$ are precisely those corresponding to the integer lattice points in the Newton polygon $\Delta_{\rho}$; equivalently, every point of $\Delta_{\rho}\cap\mathbb{Z}^2$ corresponds to a monomial with nonzero coefficient in $P_{\rho}$.

This conjecture asserts that the support of each Markov polynomial saturates its Newton polygon at all integer lattice points. The surrounding text attributes the Newton-polygon description and the conjecture to earlier work, but no resolution status is supplied here.

374452.title: Lin–Zhou's distance spectral extremal conjecture
374452.literal_statement:
Let $m\geqslant 3$, and define

$$
n:=\Bigl\lceil \tfrac{1+\sqrt{8m+1}}{2}\Bigr\rceil, \qquad s:=m-\binom{n-1}{2}\in\{1,2,\ldots,n-1\}.
$$

For positive integers $N\geqslant c\geqslant 1$, let

$$
P_{N,c} \,:=\,\bigl(c+c\lfloor N/c\rfloor - N\bigr)\,P_{\lfloor N/c\rfloor}\;\cup\;\bigl(N-c\lfloor N/c\rfloor\bigr)\,P_{\lceil N/c\rceil},
$$

the balanced disjoint union of $c$ paths on $N$ vertices. Let $\mathcal G(m)$ be the class of connected graphs with $m$ edges, and let $\rho(G)$ denote the distance spectral radius of a connected graph $G$.

**Lin–Zhou's conjecture.** If $1\leqslant s\leqslant \frac{n-7}{2}$ and $G\in\mathcal G(m)$, then

$$
\rho(G)\geqslant\rho\bigl(\overline{P_{n,s+1}}\bigr),
$$

with equality if and only if $G\cong\overline{P_{n,s+1}}$.

Lin and Zhou proved the same extremal characterization when $\max\{\frac{n-6}{2},1\}\leqslant s\leqslant n-1$; the conjecture concerns the remaining small-$s$ range and was subsequently posed in their concluding remarks.

374591.title: Wang–Zhang–Zhang's immanant conjectures for cyclic groups
374591.literal_statement:
Let $C_n$ be the cyclic group of order $n$. For a partition $lambda$ of $n$, let $mathcal I_lambda(C_n)$ denote the number of formally different monomials occurring in the immanant of the Cayley-table matrix of $C_n$. Write $mathcal P(C_n)$ and $mathcal D(C_n)$ for the corresponding quantities for the permanent and determinant, respectively.

**Wang–Zhang–Zhang's immanant conjectures.**

1. For any $n ge 3$, if $n$ is odd, then

$$
mathcal I_{(n-1,1)}(C_n)=mathcal I_{(2,1^{n-2})}(C_n)=0.
$$

2. For any $n ge 2$, if $nequiv 2pmod 4$, then

$$
mathcal I_{(n-1,1)}(C_n)=mathcal P(C_n),qquad mathcal I_{(2,1^{n-2})}(C_n)=mathcal D(C_n).
$$

3. For any $n ge 7$, if $n$ is odd, then

$$
mathcal I_{(n-2,1,1)}(C_n)=mathcal P(C_n).
$$

These conjectures extend questions about when immanant monomial counts agree with the permanent or determinant counts, and concern the behavior of these quantities for cyclic groups in the odd and $2$ modulo $4$ cases. The supplied text does not establish their status beyond presenting them as conjectures.

375055.title: Frankl–Gryaznov–Talebanfard's clique-counting conjecture for hypergraphs
375055.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be an $n$-vertex $r$-graph. A **clique** is a subset $S\subseteq V(\mathcal H)$ such that either $|S|<r$, or $|S|\ge r$ and every $r$-subset of $S$ belongs to $\mathcal{H}$. Let $k(\mathcal{H})$ be the number of cliques, and define

$$
V(x,t)=\sum_{j=0}^{t}\binom{x}{j}.
$$

**Frankl–Gryaznov–Talebanfard's conjecture.** If $\mathcal{H}$ contains no clique of size $ell+1$, then

$$
k(\mathcal H)\le V\!\left(\frac{(r-1)n}{\ell},r-1\right)^{\frac{\ell}{r-1}}.
$$

Furthermore, when $r-1\mid\ell$ and $ell\mid(r-1)n$, the unique extremal case is the $n$-vertex $ell/(r-1)$-partite $r$-graph whose edge set consists of all $r$-sets intersecting each part in at most $r-1$ vertices. This conjecture gives a sharp upper bound on the total number of cliques and specifies the equality case under the stated divisibility conditions.

375477.title: The full-degree vertex necessity conjecture for saturation of joins
375477.literal_statement:
Let $F$ be a non-empty graph and let $n\geq |V(F)|+1$. Write $K_1\vee F$ for the join of $F$ with a single vertex, and call a vertex **full-degree** if its degree is $n-1$. An **extremal graph** for saturation is an $n$-vertex $K_1\vee F$-saturated graph with $\operatorname{sat}(n,K_1\vee F)$ edges.

**Full-degree vertex necessity conjecture.** If

$$
\operatorname{sat}(n,K_1\vee F)=n-1+\operatorname{sat}(n-1,F),
$$

then some extremal graph of $K_1\vee F$ contains a full-degree vertex.

The conjecture proposes a necessary structural condition for equality in the standard upper bound obtained by adjoining a universal vertex to an extremal $F$-saturated graph. The paper's discussion shows that, for the particular join $K_1\vee(K_{p-1}^-\cup K_1)$, extremal graphs have no full-degree vertex, but it does not establish the conjecture in general.

375506.title: Frankl--Wang conjecture for non-trivial cross-intersecting families of different uniformities
375506.literal_statement:
Let $n\ge 2a\ge 2b\ge 4$, and let $A_0\in\binom{[2,n]}{a}$ and $B_0\in\binom{[2,n]}{b}$ satisfy $A_0\cap B_0\ne\emptyset$. Define

$$
\mathcal{A}_0=\{A_0\}\cup\{A\in\binom{[n]}{a}:1\in A,\ A\cap B_0\ne\emptyset\},
$$

$$
\mathcal{B}_0=\{B_0\}\cup\{B\in\binom{[n]}{b}:1\in B,\ B\cap A_0\ne\emptyset\}.
$$

Two families are **cross-intersecting** if every member of one intersects every member of the other, and are **non-trivial** if neither family is a star. **Frankl--Wang's conjecture.** If $\mathcal{A}\subset\binom{[n]}{a}$ and $\mathcal{B}\subset\binom{[n]}{b}$ are non-trivial cross-intersecting families, then

$$
|\mathcal{A}||\mathcal{B}|\le |\mathcal{A}_0||\mathcal{B}_0|.
$$

This proposes the cross-Hilton--Milner-type pair as the extremal construction when the two families have different uniformities. The supplied source does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.

$$
\mathcal{A}_0=\{A_0\}\cup\{A\in\binom{[n]}{a}:1\in A,\ A\cap B_0\ne\emptyset\},
$$

$$
\mathcal{B}_0=\{B_0\}\cup\{B\in\binom{[n]}{b}:1\in B,\ B\cap A_0\ne\emptyset\}.
$$

Two families are **cross-intersecting** if every member of one intersects every member of the other, and are **non-trivial** if neither family is a star. **Frankl--Wang's conjecture.** If $\mathcal{A}\subset\binom{[n]}{a}$ and $\mathcal{B}\subset\binom{[n]}{b}$ are non-trivial cross-intersecting families, then

$$
|\mathcal{A}||\mathcal{B}|\le |\mathcal{A}_0||\mathcal{B}_0|.
$$

This proposes the cross-Hilton--Milner-type pair as the extremal construction when the two families have different uniformities. The supplied source does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.

375516.title: Global monotonicity conjecture for the Kubo–Mori update
375516.literal_statement:
Let $X$ be the observed evidence, let $\mathcal{E}$ be the quantum channel, and let $\sigma$ be the current density matrix. Write $\mathcal{L}_X(\sigma)$ for the log-likelihood and define the full Kubo–Mori update by

$$
\sigma_+=\mathcal{R}^{\text{KM}}_{\sigma,\mathcal{E}}(X).
$$

**Global monotonicity conjecture.** The Kubo–Mori update can only increase the log-likelihood:

$$
\mathcal{L}_X(\sigma_+)\geqslant\mathcal{L}_X(\sigma).
$$

Equality holds if and only if $\sigma$ is a fixed point of the Kubo–Mori update, namely $\sigma_+=\sigma$.

The preceding local increase theorem establishes strict improvement for sufficiently small step sizes whenever the Riemannian gradient is nonzero. The conjecture asserts the stronger global statement for the full multiplicative update with step size $\eta=1$; its resolution is not supplied in the source.

375579.title: Matsubara-Heo–Telen local-multiplicity conjecture for principal matroid determinants
375579.literal_statement: Let $L\subseteq\mathbb{P}^n$ be a linear subspace of dimension $d$ not contained in any coordinate hyperplane, let $M=\operatorname{M}(L)$, and let $F$ be a flat of $M$. Write $L|_F$ for the restriction associated with $F$, let $(L|_F^{-1})^\vee$ be its projective dual, and let $E_L$ be the principal matroid determinant. Let $L^{-2}$ denote the image of $L^{-1}$ under the coordinate-wise squaring map. **Matsubara-Heo–Telen's local-multiplicity conjecture.** For each flat $F$ of $M$ such that $(L|_F^{-1})^\vee$ is a hypersurface, the defining polynomial of that hypersurface appears in the factorization of $E_L$ with exponent equal to the local multiplicity of $L^{-2}$ along the stratum indexed by $F$. This conjecture specifies the multiplicities of dual-variety factors in the principal matroid determinant; the source states that the conjectures motivating the paper were left open.

376038.title: Hopkins's rowmotion cyclic sieving meta-conjecture
376038.literal_statement:
Let $P$ be a finite graded poset of rank $r$ for which the roots of $\aΩ_P(m)$ are all integers or half-integers, and in the latter case possessing an order two automorphism. Let $m \a0geq 1$ be an integer and define

$$
\Omega_P(m;q):= \prod_{\alpha} \frac{1-q^{\kappa(m-\alpha)}}{1-q^{-\kappa \alpha}},
$$

a product over all the roots $\alpha$ of $\Omega_P(m)$ with multiplicity, and with $\kappa:= 1$ if the roots are integers or $\kappa:= 2$ if they are half-integers. **Hopkins's rowmotion cyclic sieving meta-conjecture.** Then $\Omega_P(m;q)$ is a polynomial in $q$ with nonnegative integer coefficients, and

$$
(\mathcal{PP}^m(P),\langle \mathrm{Row} \rangle \simeq \mathbb{Z}/\kappa(r+2)\mathbb{Z},\Omega_P(m;q))
$$

exhibits cyclic sieving. This predicts a uniform cyclic sieving phenomenon for rowmotion on $P$-partitions; the paper recalls several proved families and establishes the staircase case, while the general assertion remains open.

376263.title: A recurrent relation for the oscillator specialization of the c(2)-weight system
376263.literal_statement:
Suppose that $\xi(G)$ is a 4-invariant of graphs extending the specialization of the $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$-weight system at $c=-\frac{3}{32}$. Let $G$ be a graph, let $x$ be a vertex of degree $2$, and let $A=\{a_1,a_2\}$ be its neighbors. Write $G_x$ for the graph obtained by deleting $x$, $\overline{G}_x$ for the graph obtained by deleting $x$ and inverting the edge $(a_1,a_2)$, and $G_x^{a_1}$ for the graph obtained from $G_x$ by applying the 2T transform to $(a_1,a_2)$ and deleting $a_1$. **The recurrent relation conjecture.** The following relation holds:

$$
\xi(G)=\left(-\frac{3}{32}-1\right)\xi(G_x)-\frac{1}{2}\xi(\overline{G}_x)+\frac{1}{2}\cdot\left(-\frac{3}{32}\right)\xi(G_x^{a_1}).
$$

This would provide a recurrence for the conjectural 4-invariant extending the $c=-\frac{3}{32}$ specialization, whose existence is motivated by the oscillator representation of $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$.

382084.title: Euler partition inequalities involving $Q_2(n)$
382084.literal_statement:
For $n,k\geqslant0$, let $p(n)$ denote Euler's partition function, let $Q_2(n)$ denote the partition function used in the source, and let $(\rho_j)_{j\geqslant0}$ be the coefficient sequence appearing in the preceding truncated-series definition. **Euler partition inequalities.**

$$
\sum_{j=0}^{3k}\rho_jp\bigl(n-j(j+1)\bigr)\geqslant Q_2(n),
$$

with strict inequality if $n\geqslant(3k+1)(3k+2)$, and

$$
\sum_{j=0}^{3k+1}\rho_jp\bigl(n-j(j+1)\bigr)\leqslant Q_2(n),
$$

with strict inequality if $n\geqslant(3k+2)(3k+3)$.

These inequalities are presented as a combinatorial interpretation of the preceding coefficient conjectures and would provide infinite families of linear inequalities for partition functions; they remain open.

382095.title: Abdollahi–Akbari–Maimani order conjecture for non-commuting graphs
382095.literal_statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be non-abelian finite groups. For a finite non-abelian group $K$, let $\Gamma_K$ be the graph whose vertices are the non-central elements of $K$, with two vertices adjacent when they do not commute. **Abdollahi–Akbari–Maimani order conjecture.** If

$$
\Gamma_G\cong\Gamma_H,
$$

then

$$
|G|=|H|.
$$

The conjecture concerns whether the non-commuting graph determines the order of a finite group. It is known for $p$-groups, dihedral groups, and simple groups, but remains open in general; the source also notes that it suffices to establish it for finite AC-groups.

382096.title: Abdollahi–Akbari–Maimani nilpotency conjecture for non-commuting graphs
382096.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite non-abelian nilpotent group, and let $H$ be a group. For a finite non-abelian group $K$, let $\Gamma_K$ be the graph whose vertices are the non-central elements of $K$, with two vertices adjacent when they do not commute. **Abdollahi–Akbari–Maimani nilpotency conjecture.** If

$$
\Gamma_G\cong\Gamma_H,
$$

then $H$ is nilpotent. This conjecture asks whether nilpotency can be recovered from the non-commuting graph. The source states that it remains open, although it is proved for finite AC-groups when $|Z(G)|\geq|Z(H)|$ and substantial partial results are known.

382097.title: Nilpotent-factor conjecture for non-commuting graphs
382097.literal_statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, and suppose that $G=P\times A$ is a finite group, where $P\in\operatorname{Syl}_p(G)$ is non-abelian and $A$ is an abelian $p'$-group. Let $\Gamma_K$ denote the non-commuting graph of a finite non-abelian group $K$, whose vertices are the non-central elements and whose edges join pairs of noncommuting vertices. **Nilpotent-factor conjecture.** If $H$ is finite,

$$
\Gamma_G\cong\Gamma_H\quad\text{and}\quad |Z(G)|\geq|Z(H)|,
$$

then $H=Q\times B$, where $q$ is a prime, $Q\in\operatorname{Syl}_q(H)$ is non-abelian, and $B$ is an abelian $q'$-group. In particular, $H$ is nilpotent. This is proposed as a reduction for the unresolved nilpotency conjecture in the case where the nilpotent group has a unique non-abelian Sylow subgroup.

382248.title: Eoh–Choi's corona-free characterization conjecture for graph grabbing
382248.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a graph with a weight function $w\colon V(G)\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ whose codomain is $\{0,1\}$. Let $\mathcal{C}_\text{odd}$ be the family of corona products of an odd cycle and a point. A graph is **$\mathcal{C}_\text{odd}$-free** if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to a member of $\mathcal{C}_\text{odd}$. **Eoh–Choi's conjecture.** Alice wins the graph-grabbing game if and only if $G$ is $\mathcal{C}_\text{odd}$-free. Eoh and Choi proved the forward implication under the stated $\{0,1\}$-valued weighting setting; the conjecture asserts the converse as well and remains open.

382260.title: Gago–Coroničová-Hurajová–Madaras conjecture on low-betweenness uniform graphs
382260.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a **low-betweenness BUG**, meaning a betweenness-uniform graph whose betweenness value is less than $1$. Write $\overline{G}$ for its complement. **Gago–Coroničová-Hurajová–Madaras conjecture.** If $G$ is a low-betweenness BUG, then its complement $\overline{G}$ is a disjoint union of stars of the same size. This would classify the low-betweenness betweenness-uniform graphs and show that the construction from disjoint unions of equally sized stars yields all such examples. The conjecture is presented as open in the source.
